subject: HaloAI comparative inference economics & next experiments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cho <alex.cho@haloai.com>, Tanya Lopez <tanya.lopez@haloai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 May 2028 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: HaloAI call recap — comparative inference economics & next experiments

Alex / Tanya — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from Redwood side and a proposed, lightweight experimental plan so we can quantify the economics delta vs the hyperscaler path you mentioned.

Key notes from the discovery:
- Primary goal: figure out per-1M token unit economics for the critical QA / assistant workload you showed (avg prompt 180 tokens, avg completion 320 tokens).
- Constraints: need sub-200ms p50 for short prompts, and predictable burst capacity for peak business hours; procurement will need cost apples-to-apples for committed vs on-demand.

What we heard makes sense. Proposed next tests (we can run or co-run, whichever you prefer):
1) Baseline run: 100k requests (distribution matched to your traffic) to measure p50/p95/p99 and raw throughput.
2) Cache hit simulation: run same workload with KV prefix hits at 0%, 30%, 60% to show unit cost sensitivity.
3) Batching sweep: measure end-to-end latency and effective tokens/sec at batch sizes {1,4,8,16} to show batching tradeoffs.
4) 1M token cost estimate: normalize to per-1M tokens including GPU time, networking, and any autoscaling overheads; present both hosted (our API) and private-dedicated runs.

Attachments: I attached today’s demo logs we captured (haloai-demo-logs.csv) and a quick 1M-token sketch (1Mtoken-econ-estimate.xlsx) — these are starter artifacts.

Asks / next steps:
- Can you share a 30–60 minute sample trace (request + reference completion) or an S3 link to anonymized request samples?
- Are you open to Redwood running the baseline + cache hit matrix on our side (we’ll share the exact test harness) or would you prefer to do it in your environment?
- Tentative timeslot: Thu May 11 — 10:00–11:00 PT (demo + walk-through of results).

I’ll loop Marissa on differentiation notes and Jordan on pricing options for a short pilot/commit.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Test matrix (we’ll provide the harness + exact TF/NGINX configs):
- Variant A (hosted): Redwood hosted API, model v1 (FP16), batch sizes 1/4/8/16, cache hits 0/30/60%.
- Variant B (dedicated): Redwood Dedicated on single-tenant GPU (NVIDIA H100-equivalent), same model/quantization sweep (FP16, 8-bit nf4), measure cost delta with reserved capacity assumptions.
- Variant C (hyperscaler baseline): synthetic baseline from hyperscaler claims using the same request distribution (we’ll try to match their published instance types).

Metrics we’ll return: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, effective cost per 1M tokens (split by compute + infra), and an annex showing tail behavior with bursts.

Attachments here are the two files I mentioned earlier (demo logs + 1M token sketch). I also uploaded the harness to the Drive link in the metadata so you can reproduce.

Marissa / Jordan — can you add short bullets on the product differentiators we should highlight and any pilot pricing concession we can offer for a two-week measurement pilot? Jordan — a line item for a $Xk trial credit and a path to a 3-month reserve would be great.

Alex / team — adding a few concise differentiation points we should surface in the test report and demo: 

- Routing & fallbacks: Redwood supports policy-driven routing (latency-first vs cost-first) with automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants when capacity is constrained — this materially improves availability vs single-cloud endpoints.
- Cache-first unit economics: our KV / prefix caching reduces token counts on typical assistant workloads by 20–60% depending on prompt reuse; capturing operating hit rate is critical for realistic TCO.
- Quantization + kernel selection: we pick quantization profiles dynamically with optimized kernels for H100/consumer-equivalent hardware which preserves latency while lowering compute cost vs naive 8-bit runs.
- Private & dedicated options: for regulated customers you can run our private control plane or Dedicated pool (predictable throughput, audits).

Suggested experiments to highlight gap vs hyperscaler: run the 60% cache-hit scenario and show per-1M token delta across three batch sizes (1,4,8). Capture both steady-state and burst tail.

On pricing: Jordan — agree on offering a two-week pilot credit that covers the test run and lets HaloAI validate results with zero risk. Recommend $15k trial credit + standard conversion discount if they commit to a 3-month reserved tier within 30 days.

-Marissa
